problem.question: Bob is tilling a plot of his garden. The plot is 110 feet wide by 120 feet long. His tiller digs a swath two feet wide, and he can till 1 foot of ground in about 2 seconds. How long will it take him to till this plot of land, in minutes?
problem.answer:
If Bob goes along the side that's 120 feet long, he will till 110 / 2 = 55 rows.
Each of these rows are 120 feet long, so he will push the tiller a total of 120 * 55 = <<120*55=6600>>6,600 feet.
He tills 1 linear foot of ground every 2 seconds, so it will take him 2 * 6,600 = 13,200 seconds to till this plot
13,200 seconds is 13,2000 / 60 = <<13200/60=220>>220 minutes
#### 220

generation.text:
First find the area of the plot: 110 feet * 120 feet = 13,200 square feet
Then divide that area by the width of the swath to find the length of ground Bob needs to till: 13,200 square feet / 2 feet = 6,600 feet
Then divide that length by the rate at which Bob tills the ground to find how long it takes him: 6,600 feet / 2 seconds/foot = 3300 seconds
Then divide that time by the number of seconds per minute to find the time in minutes: 3300 seconds / 60 seconds/minute = 55 minutes
The final answer is \boxed{55}.
